sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
subiere: subeō, -īre, -iī, -itum — to go under, come beneath (3rd pl. perf., = subiērunt)
subita: subitus, -a, -um — sudden, unexpected (f. abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
summas: summus, -a, -um — highest, topmost; surface of (f. acc. pl.)
super: super (adv. and prep.) — above, over; besides, in addition · also remaining, left over (sōla mei super imāgō)
supera: superō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to overcome, surmount, win over (imperative sg.)
superque: super (adv., prep.) — above, over; satis superque, enough and more than enough + -que, and
suprema: suprēmus, -a, -um — highest, last, extreme (superl. of superus; f. nom./abl. sg.; n. pl.)
suscipiunt: suscipiō, -ere, -cēpī, -ceptum — to take up, catch, support, receive (3rd pl. pres.)
taedis: taeda, -ae (f.) — pine-wood, pine torch, resinous plank (abl. pl.; also dat. pl.)
talis: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (f. acc. pl., -is for -ēs) · also m./f. nom. sg. (talis erat Dido)
tantum: tantus, -a, -um — so great; tantum (n. acc. sg.), so great a thing; (adv.) only, so much · also m. acc. sg. (tantum dolorem)
tendere: tendō, -ere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch, direct one's course, make for (pres. inf.)
tenebris: tenebrae, -ārum (f. pl.) — darkness, gloom, shadows (abl./dat. pl.)
tenet: teneō, tenēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, occupy (3rd sg. pres.)
tenuere: teneō, tenēre, tenuī — to hold, occupy, keep (3rd pl. perf., = tenuērunt)
tenues: tenuis, -e — thin, slight, scanty, poor (m./f. nom./acc. pl.)
terra: terra, -ae (f.) — land, earth, ground (nom./abl. sg.) · also f. voc. sg. (ō terra hospita)
teucri: Teucer, Teucrī (m.) — Teucer, early king of Troy (gen. sg.) · also Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) Trojans (voc. pl.: Teucrī, secludite) · also m. nom. pl. (Teucrī, Trojans)
texit: tegō, -ere, tēxī, tēctum — to cover, hide, shelter, protect (3rd sg. perf.)
thalami: thalamus, -ī (m.) — bedchamber, marriage-chamber (nom. pl.; also gen. sg.)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
triste: tristis, -e — grim, sad, bitter (n. acc. sg.)
tristisque: tristis, -e — sad, grim (f. acc. pl., -is for -ēs) + -que 'and'
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
tuta: tūtus, -a, -um — safe, sheltered (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom./abl. sg.)
ultrices: ultrix, ultrīcis — avenging; as f. noun, an avenger (f. nom. pl.; also f. acc. pl.)
umbra: umbra, -ae (f.) — shade, shadow (abl. sg.; nom. sg.)
umbrae: umbra, -ae (f.) — shadow, shade (nom. pl.; gen./dat. sg.)
umbraeque: umbra, -ae (f.) — shade, ghost, shadow (nom. pl.) + -que, and
undantia: undō, -āre, -āvī — to surge, billow, ripple (pres. part., n. nom./acc. pl.)
vana: vānus, -a, -um — empty, false, idle (f. abl. sg.; f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
vastoque: vastus, -a, -um — vast, empty, desolate (m./n. abl./dat. sg.) + -que 'and'
venere: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come (3 pl. perf., = vēnērunt)
venientibus: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come; veniēns (pres. part., m./f./n. dat./abl. pl.)
vestro: vester, vestra, vestrum — your (pl.) (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
viri: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero, husband (nom. pl.; gen. sg.) · also voc. pl. (festīnāte, virī)
viridi: viridis, -e — green, fresh (m./n. abl. sg.) · also f. abl. sg. (virīdī olīvā)
viscera: viscus, vīsceris (n.) — flesh; pl. viscera, entrails (acc. pl.)
visu: vīsus, -ūs (m.) — sight, seeing (abl. sg.; miserābile vīsū, pitiable to see)
volgo: vulgus (volgus), -ī (n.) — the crowd; volgō (abl. sg. as adv.), commonly, everywhere
volitare: volitō, -āre — to fly about, flit, flutter (pres. inf.)
